text: Train cardiovascular endurance and leg strength well in advance, and simulate carrying a loaded pack on varied terrain.
Inspect and test all technical gear, including ropes, harnesses, and crampons, before departure and again at base camp.
Check multiple forecast sources and understand how local topography can alter weather patterns on the mountain.
Study the route in detail, identify escape options, and set clear turnaround times before leaving camp.
Carry a first-aid kit, communication device, and a clear emergency plan known to every member of the team.
Pack out all waste, minimise campsite impact, and respect wildlife and local communities near the mountain.
Establish check-in times with a base contact and carry a satellite communicator where cellular coverage is unavailable.
Agree on decision-making processes in advance, and empower any member to call for a turnaround if conditions warrant.
Respect permit systems, local guiding regulations, and the cultural significance many mountains hold for local communities.
